thread.title: Dow futures retreat as government shutdown stretches into 3rd day

author: Victor Reklaitis
title: Dow futures retreat as government shutdown stretches into 3rd day
text:
U.S. stock futures on Monday pointed to a step lower at the open as a partial government shutdown stretched into a third day.
Strategists are saying shutdowns can weigh on the stock market, but they don’t tend to bring about heavy selling.
What are the main benchmarks doing? 
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures YMH8, -0.19% fell by 52 points, or 0.2%, to 25,994, while S&P 500 futures ESH8, -0.10% shed 3.50 points, or 0.1%, to 2,807.50. Nasdaq-100 futures NQH8, -0.03% lost 5.25 points, or 0.1%, to 6,840.50.
On Friday, the S&P 500 SPX, +0.44% and Nasdaq Composite COMP, +0.55% scored all-time closing highs , while the Dow DJIA, +0.21% rose to within 0.2% of its record close that was achieved Wednesday. The three gauges have gained between 24% and 32% over the past 12 months, helped by an expanding U.S. economy, growth in corporate profits and enthusiasm over tax cuts for companies .
What are strategists saying? 
“History says that investors have little to fear from government shutdowns, as four of the seven in the past 35 years were accompanied by price declined that averaged only 1.0% and required less than two weeks to get back to break even,” said Sam Stovall, CFRA’s chief investment strategist, in a note late Sunday. 
“We think this shutdown will also be a non-event,” Stovall added.
See: This is what happens in the stock market when the government shuts down 
And read: A shutdown ‘could reintroduce investors to the fact that markets go down’ 
What’s driving markets? 
Shutdown-related uncertainty appears to be weighing on markets. Lawmakers failed Sunday to end the federal government shutdown, as negotiations over immigration continued to roil Capitol Hill.
The Senate was expected to hold a procedural vote at noon Eastern Time on a measure that would keep the government funded through Feb. 8, but it wasn’t clear if it would have enough support to advance.
Economic reports could be overshadowed or even be delayed this week by the shutdown, but a reading on the Chicago Federal Reserve’s national activity index was still due at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time.
Check out: MarketWatch’s Economic Calendar 
Which stocks look like key movers? 
Apple Inc. ’s stock AAPL, -0.45% traded 0.9% lower in premarket trading. The dip comes amid fresh concerns about iPhone X sales, with the worries weighing on the Silicon Valley giant’s suppliers in Asia .
Shares in oil-field services provider Halliburton Co. HAL, +1.24% and broker TD Ameritrade Holding Corp. AMTD, +0.38% could see active trading as they are among the companies expected to post earnings before the open, while streaming-video pioneer Netflix Inc. NFLX, +0.06% is due to report after the close.

And read: As stocks rocket to records, Ameritrade to roll out round-the-clock trade 
What are other assets doing? 
The ICE U.S. Dollar Index DXY, -0.09% was modestly lower as traders waited for developments on the shutdown. European stocks SXXP, +0.01% were little changed, and Asian markets closed mostly higher . Gold futures GCG8, +0.05% and oil futures CLG8, +0.14% were little changed.
